$$

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,x(0),

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $x(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$

$$

decision.explanation: Multiplying the given matrix exponential by (0,-1)^T gives x(t)=-sinh(7t) and y(t)=-cosh(7t). Their derivatives satisfy x'=7y and y'=7x, and their initial values are 0 and -1.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=7y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=7x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(0) \\ y(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
after.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,x(0),
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $x(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ -\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $x(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sinh}⁡(7t) \\ -\operatorname{cosh}⁡(7t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=5y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(2) \\ y(2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
after.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c,
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t-2)}\,x(2) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-2)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-2)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-2)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-2))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-2)) \\ -\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-2))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=5y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(2) \\ y(2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5t) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
content.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c,
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t-2)}\,x(2) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-2)) & \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-2)) \\ \operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-2)) & \operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-2))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cosh}⁡(5(t-2)) \\ -\operatorname{sinh}⁡(5(t-2))\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}$

$\text{L6}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,x(0)$

Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}.$ Since ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is a fundamental matrix for the system, every solution of the system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c\,\text{for some constant vector }c.
$$

Thus, $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by the $\text{properties of a fundamental matrix}.$

- Next, we consider line $\text{L4}.$ By definition, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ satisfies the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.

The second condition here is exactly line $\text{L4},$ so $\text{L4}$ follows from the definition of ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ as the standard fundamental matrix by $\text{using the initial condition }{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.$

$$
x(t)={e}^{At}\,x(0).
$$

Thus, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L2}$ and substitution from $\text{L1}\text{ and }\text{L5}.$
